([[Winterville, North Carolina]]) * [[Montverde Academy]]
([[Montverde, Florida]]) | college = [[North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball|North Carolina]] (2020–2021) | draft_year = 2021 | draft_round = 1 | draft_pick = 29 | draft_team = [[Phoenix Suns]] | career_start = 2021 | years1 = {{nbay|2021|start}}–present | team1 = [[Brooklyn Nets]] | years2 = [[2021–22 NBA G League season|2021]]–[[2022–23 NBA G League season|2023]] | team2 = →[[Long Island Nets]] | highlights = * [[Atlantic Coast Conference|ACC]] All-Freshman Team (2021) * [[McDonald's All-American Game|McDonald's All-American]] ([[2020 McDonald's All-American Boys Game|2020]]) }} '''Day'Ron Yusha Sharpe''' (born November 6, 2001) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Brooklyn Nets]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He played [[college basketball]] for the [[North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball|North Carolina Tar Heels]]. ==Early life== Sharpe began his high school career playing for [[South Central High School (North Carolina)|South Central High School]] in [[Winterville, North Carolina]]. As a sophomore, he averaged 14.3 points and 9.3 rebounds per game.{{cite news |last1=Pope |first1=Jonas |title=What kind of player is UNC getting in big man Day'Ron Sharpe? |url=https://www.charlotteobserver.com/sports/college/article213390014.html |access-date=December 1, 2020 |work=[[Charlotte Observer]] |date=June 18, 2018}} Sharpe averaged 16.5 points and 10.7 rebounds per game as a junior, helping South Central finish with a 30–1 record and win the NCHSAA Class 4A state title. He announced he was transferring to [[Montverde Academy]] for his senior season.{{cite news |last1=Pope |first1=Jonas |title=UNC 2020 basketball commit, Day'Ron Sharpe to transfer |url=https://www.newsobserver.com/sports/college/acc/unc/article233272213.html |access-date=December 1, 2020 |work=[[The News & Observer]] |date=July 29, 2019}} Sharpe averaged 12.1 points and 7.3 rebounds per game as a senior, leading Montverde to a 25–0 record and No. 1 national ranking according to MaxPreps.{{cite web |last1=Jones |first1=Andrew |last2=King |first2=Deana |title=The Final Book On Day'Ron Sharpe |url=https://northcarolina.rivals.com/news/the-final-book-on-day-ron-sharpe |website=[[Rivals.com]] |access-date=December 1, 2020 |date=April 11, 2020}} He was named a [[McDonald's All-American Game|McDonald's All-American]] as well as a [[Jordan Brand Classic|Jordan Brand All-American]].{{cite news |last1=McMillan |first1=Sherrell |title=Four UNC Signees Named McDonald's All-Americans |url=https://247sports.com/college/north-carolina/Article/Four-UNC-Basketball-Signees-Named-McDonalds-All-Americans-142517274/ |access-date=December 1, 2020 |work=247 Sports |date=January 23, 2020}}{{cite news |last1=Martin |first1=Ross |title=Three UNC Signees Named to Jordan Brand All-Star Game |url=https://247sports.com/article/three-unc-signees-named-to-jordan-brand-all-star-game-143832932/ |access-date=December 1, 2020 |work=247 Sports |date=February 15, 2020}} In AAU play, he played for Garner Road.{{cite news |last1=Jordan |first1=Jason |title=adidas Gauntlet: UNC commit Day'Ron Sharpe motivated to kickoff spring/summer ball |url=https://usatodayhss.com/2019/adidas-gauntlet-unc-commit-dayron-sharpe-motivated-to-kickoff-spring-summer-ball |access-date=December 1, 2020 |work=[[USA Today]] |date=April 13, 2019}} Sharpe was considered a five-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] ranked the No. 5 center in the class of 2020 and the No. 22 overall player by [[247Sports]]. He committed to [[North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball|North Carolina]] on June 17, 2018, becoming the first member of the class of 2020 to commit to the Tar Heels. Sharpe turned down scholarship offers from [[Virginia Cavaliers men's basketball|Virginia]], [[East Carolina Pirates men's basketball|East Carolina]] and [[Georgetown Hoyas men's basketball|Georgetown]]. {{College Athlete Recruit Start|40=no|collapse=no|year=2020}} {{College Athlete Recruit Entry | recruit = Day'Ron Sharpe | position = [[Center (basketball)|C]] | hometown = [[Greenville, North Carolina|Greenville, NC]] | highschool = [[Montverde Academy]] (FL) | feet = 6 | inches = 10 | weight = 246 | 40 = | commitdate = June 17, 2018 | scout stars = | rivals stars = 5 | 247 stars = 5 | espn stars = 5 | espn grade = 94 }} {{College Athlete Recruit End | 40 = | year = 2020 | rivals ref title = North Carolina 2020 Basketball Commitments | scout ref title = | espn ref title = 2020 North Carolina Tar Heels Recruiting Class | rivals school = northcarolina | scout s = | espn schoolid = 153 | 247 overall = 22 | rivals overall = 13 | espn overall = 12 | accessdate = December 1, 2020 | bball = yes }} ==College career== In Sharpe's freshman debut on November 25, 2020, he had 13 points and 10 rebounds in a 79–60 win against [[College of Charleston Cougars men's basketball|College of Charleston]].{{cite news |title=Freshmen lead No. 16 UNC past College of Charleston 79–60 |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401252794 |access-date=December 1, 2020 |work=[[ESPN]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=November 25, 2020}} He became the fourth [[North Carolina]] player to record a double-double in his debut game, joining [[Lennie Rosenbluth]], [[Sam Perkins]], and [[Cole Anthony]].{{cite news |last1=Brown |first1=C.L. |title=UNC basketball: Day'Ron Sharpe gives North Carolina's frontcourt an edge |url=https://www.newsobserver.com/sports/college/acc/unc/article246969592.html |access-date=December 1, 2020 |work=[[The News & Observer]] |date=November 25, 2020}} Sharpe averaged 9.5 points and 7.6 rebounds per game as a freshman. On March 24, 2021, Sharpe declared for the [[2021 NBA draft]].{{cite news |last1=Boone |first1=Kyle|title=2021 NBA Draft: North Carolina's Day'Ron Sharpe declares as potential first-round selection |url=https://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/news/2021-nba-draft-north-carolinas-dayron-sharpe-declares-as-potential-first-round-selection/ |access-date=July 6, 2021 |work=[[CBS Sports]] |date=March 24, 2021}} ==Professional career== === Brooklyn Nets (2021–present) === Sharpe was selected with the 29th pick in the [[2021 NBA draft]] by the [[Phoenix Suns]].{{cite news |last1=Brown |first1=C.L. |title=Former UNC standout Day'Ron Sharpe selected in NBA draft by championship contender |url=https://www.newsobserver.com/sports/college/acc/unc/article253114453.html |access-date=July 31, 2021 |work=[[The News & Observer]] |date=July 29, 2021}} On August 6, 2021, [[Jevon Carter]] and the draft rights to Sharpe were traded to the [[Brooklyn Nets]] in exchange for [[Landry Shamet]].{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/nets/news/2021/08/06/brooklyn-nets-acquire-jevon-carter-draft-rights-dayron-sharpe-phoenix-suns|title=BROOKLYN NETS ACQUIRE JEVON CARTER, DRAFT RIGHTS TO DAY'RON SHARPE FROM PHOENIX SUNS|work=NBA.com|date=August 6, 2021}} On January 13, 2022, the Nets beat the [[2021–22 Chicago Bulls season|Chicago Bulls]] 138–112. In this game, Sharpe played 21 minutes, made 10 of 14 shots, scored 20 points, had seven rebounds and one block. The 20 points in this game set a new personal season–high (his previous record was 14 points, against the [[2021–22 Portland Trail Blazers season|Portland Trail Blazers]] on January 11). On January 10, 2024, Sharpe was diagnosed with hyperextension of his left knee, according to Nets reporter Brian Lewis. He had suffered the injury during a January 8 against the Trail Blazers, and was scheduled to be re-evaluated in two weeks time.https://www.netsdaily.com/2024/1/9/24031598/dayron-sharpe-diagnosed-with-hype-extended-left-knee Day’Ron Sharpe diagnosed with hyper-extended left knee, out at least two weeks In a March 19 game against the [[2023–24 New Orleans Pelicans season|New Orleans Pelicans]], Sharpe played 23 minutes and shot 4-for-11 from the field, registering 8 points, a career-high 17 rebounds (previously 15 on December 21, 2023 against the [[2023–24 New York Knicks season|New York Knicks]]), three assists, and two blocks. Sharpe made 50 appearances (two starts) for the Nets during the [[2024–25 NBA season]], averaging 7.9 points, 6.6 rebounds, and 1.8 assists. On June 30, 2025, Sharpe re-signed with the Nets on a two-year, $12 million contract.{{cite web |last=Charania |first=Shams |author-link=Shams Charania |date=2025-06-30 |title=Sources: Williams, Sharpe to re-sign with Nets |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/45617183/sources-ziaire-williams-stay-nets-2-year-12m-deal |access-date=2025-12-06 |website=ESPN.com}} Sharpe made 62 appearances (including seven starts) for the Nets during the [[2025–26 NBA season|2025–26 season]], recording averages of 8.7 points, 6.7 rebounds, and 2.3 assists. On March 12, 2026, it was announced that Sharpe would require season-ending surgery to repair a torn [[ulnar collateral ligament of thumb|ulnar collateral ligament]] in his left thumb.{{Cite
